jobs.title: Research Assistant at CSUN 24200 - Autonomy Research Center for STEAHM
jobs.description: Employer: CSUN 24200 - Autonomy Research Center for STEAHM Expires: 12/02/2026 Research Assistant — Convergence Research, Innovation, and Societal Impact Book ProjectPosition: Undergraduate or Graduate Research AssistantFaculty Lead: Dr. Nhut Tan HoSenior Advisor: Dr. Peter GrayProject: Convergence in Action: How Deep Integration Across Disciplines and Sectors Turns Complex Problems into Innovation and Societal ImpactHours: Approximately 10 hours/week, depending on assignmentCompensation and duration: $18/hour and academic year, with possibility of continuation Project DescriptionStudents are invited to participate in the research and development of a book examining how universities, government, industry, and other organizations work across disciplinary and institutional boundaries to address complex societal and technological problems.The book will draw on case studies from the National Science Foundation's convergence research programs, selected MIT and other universities’ initiatives, and the NASA-sponsored Autonomy Research Center for STEAHM (ARCS) at CSUN. It will investigate not only what these projects accomplished, but how successful convergence efforts are designed and operated.Major questions include:What distinguishes genuine convergence from conventional interdisciplinary research?How are effective cross-disciplinary and cross-sector teams created?How are complex societal problems identified and framed?How do teams integrate different disciplines, methods, and perspectives?How do government, industry, communities, and end users participate?What organizational barriers prevent convergence?How does research move toward innovation and societal impact?What institutional practices make convergence sustainable?Student Responsibilities:Depending on interests and background, research assistants may participate in one or more of the following:research NSF-funded convergence projects and investigators;collect and verify project information from authoritative sources;search scholarly literature, reports, project websites, publications, patents, and other evidence of outcomes;develop structured case-study research dossiers;analyze how multidisciplinary teams were formed and operated;identify evidence of research translation and societal impact;conduct background research on interview subjects;assist in preparing interview questions;organize and analyze interview transcripts;code interviews and cases for recurring themes and lessons learned;maintain bibliographic records and research databases;research MIT and other institutional convergence models;document lessons from ARCS projects and participants;prepare concise research summaries, tables, timelines, and visual materials;support fact-checking, references, and manuscript development.Students will not simply summarize sources. They will be trained to analyze each case using a common framework:Problem → Team → Integration → Stakeholders → Translation → Outcomes → LessonsDesired QualificationsStrong candidates will have:intellectual curiosity and interest in research, innovation, technology, or societal problems;strong reading and analytical skills;careful attention to evidence and accuracy;ability to summarize complex material clearly;reliability and ability to work independently;strong written English;comfort learning topics outside their primary discipline.Students from all disciplines are encouraged to apply, including engineering, computer science, social sciences, humanities, business, health sciences, communication, design, and education.Prior research experience is helpful but not required.Particularly Valuable SkillsExperience with any of the following is useful:literature searches;qualitative research;interview analysis;data organization;Zotero or other reference-management software;Excel/Google Sheets;bibliographic databases;visualization;AI-assisted research tools used responsibly;technical or science writing.What Students Will LearnStudents will gain experience in:convergence and interdisciplinary research;science and innovation policy;qualitative and case-study research;scholarly literature review;analysis of large research programs;interviewing and qualitative coding;research translation and societal-impact assessment;working directly with faculty and national research leaders.Students may also have opportunities to participate in conversations with researchers, government program leaders, university leaders, and other experts involved in major convergence initiatives.ApplicationInterested students should submit their application package below to this link https://forms.gle/6GaGcmpLwyqb28F48 :a brief statement of interest (approximately 250 words);résumé/CV;academic major and year;description of any relevant research, writing, data, or analytical experience;one example of a complex problem or project that interests you and why you think multiple disciplines would be needed to address it.

Asset Management is responsible for the tagging and tracking of all University Assets from their arrival on campus through their life cycle and disposal. Central Receiving provides a point of delivery for all incoming packages to the University. jobs.title: Web Developer at CSUN 10349 - Student Affairs IT
jobs.description: Employer: CSUN 10349 - Student Affairs IT - Student Affairs Expires: 12/02/2026 Student Affairs IT is looking for a motivated student assistant with web development skills and a desire to work in a real-world web application development environment. Our team has over 40 years of combined Fortune 50 and consulting experience in the web space...you'll learn a lot here. You'll also gain highly desirable and marketable job skills, while building your portfolio and making CSUN web applications work better for everyone. We assist our grads with resume review and interview preparation, and have a pipeline to a number of employers and recruiters.Basic skills and knowledge we're looking for:One or more of the following: PHP, JavaScript, Ruby, JavaFamiliarity with relational databases and SQLFamiliarity with a MVC (Model-View-Controller) framework, i.e. Ruby on Rails, Laravel (a big plus)HTML & CSSFamiliarity with software versioning tools, i.e. git, GitHubFamiliarity with AWS infrastructure and/or the LAMP development stack (a plus)Familiarity with software development life cycle/agile web development (not required, but a plus)You should be able to demonstrate a solid working knowledge of all items listed above, because they are basic components of what you'll be doing. You should also be able to demonstrate that you have built at least one working web application. This position is geared toward the practical needs of the Student Affairs web application development environment, so you’ll be doing real work that will be seen by your peers on day one. Day-to-day activities involve code maintenance for existing applications, new application development, and working directly with clients. You should have a positive, team-oriented and enthusiastic attitude. SAIT is a fun environment; familiarity with pop culture goes a long way here.Hourly rate starts at $17.00, with a "bump" if you can demonstrate proficiency during your first 90 days with us.PLEASE NOTE:You MUST be enrolled in classes at CSUN in order to work in this position.You MUST have at least THREE semesters until graduation to be considered for this position.Qualified applicants will be asked to complete a code challenge.Openings may not be available at the time of your application.This position is 100% remote during remote instruction.
